sources.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis, 1962 (primary source collection: ExComm meeting recordings and transcripts)
sources.author_or_institution: John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum
sources.date: Recordings made Oct 1962; archive maintained ongoing
sources.supported_claim: Timeline of U-2 photo discovery (Oct 14-16), ExComm formation and deliberation, and the Oct 22 public announcement.

sources.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis, 1962 — Briefing Book (declassified ExComm transcripts, CIA and DoD documents)
sources.author_or_institution: National Security Archive, George Washington University
sources.date: Archive compiled from documents dated 1962; ongoing curation
sources.supported_claim: Details of the Oct 16-20 ExComm option debate (air strike vs. blockade), Joint Chiefs' position, and OAS/Rio Treaty legal framing of the quarantine.

sources.title: Essence of Decision: Explaining the Cuban Missile Crisis (2nd ed.)
sources.author_or_institution: Graham T. Allison and Philip Zelikow
sources.citation: Allison, G. & Zelikow, P. (1999). Essence of Decision: Explaining the Cuban Missile Crisis (2nd ed.). Longman.
sources.supported_claim: Analytical framing of the ExComm decision process as a model case of graduated, reversible crisis response; assessment of decision quality independent of outcome.

sources.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis in American Memory: Myth versus Reality
sources.citation: Stern, S. M. (2012). The Cuban Missile Crisis in American Memory: Myth versus Reality. Stanford University Press.
sources.supported_claim: Re-analysis of the ExComm tape recordings showing disagreement among participant memoirs about how unified the group was and when key figures shifted position; basis for the SOURCE_DISAGREEMENT entry on ExComm unanimity.

sources.title: Thirteen Days: A Memoir of the Cuban Missile Crisis
sources.citation: Kennedy, R. F. (1969). Thirteen Days: A Memoir of the Cuban Missile Crisis. W. W. Norton & Company.
sources.supported_claim: Robert Kennedy's own account of arguing against a surprise air strike as morally comparable to a 'Pearl Harbor in reverse.'

sources.title: CORONA and Cuba: U-2 and Photographic Intelligence in the Missile Crisis (declassified intelligence assessments)
sources.author_or_institution: Central Intelligence Agency, Freedom of Information Act Electronic Reading Room
sources.supported_claim: Contemporary CIA estimates of Soviet troop levels (~8,000-10,000) and of missile-site readiness timelines, later shown to significantly understate actual Soviet troop strength (~42,000).

sources.title: One Minute to Midnight: Kennedy, Khrushchev, and Castro on the Brink of Nuclear War
sources.citation: Dobbs, M. (2008). One Minute to Midnight. Alfred A. Knopf.
sources.supported_claim: Account of the October 27 B-59 submarine incident and Vasili Arkhipov's refusal to authorize a nuclear torpedo launch, based on interviews with surviving Soviet submarine officers and declassified Soviet naval records.

sources.title: Cuban missile crisis
sources.supported_claim: General chronology cross-check: resolution terms (missile withdrawal, non-invasion pledge, secret Jupiter-missile-in-Turkey withdrawal) and long-term consequences (hotline, 1963 Partial Test Ban Treaty).
